Wall Street economists had forecast a May trade deficit of $9.18 billion.

The value of total imports increased for a seventh consecutive month during May to hit a record $87.47 billion, the department said. Total exports fell for a second straight month, down 0.8 percent to $77.24 billion.
The department said the $3.63 billion deficit with Japan in May was the lowest in nearly a year since a $3.3 billion gap was posted in June 1996.

The $3.76 billion deficit with China was the highest since October 1996 when it reached $4.9 billion. May marked only the third month on record that the monthly trade shortfall with China outstripped the deficit with Japan.
The $1.70 billion May deficit with Mexico was a record, while the shortfall with Canada more than doubled, rising 104.1 percent to $1.74 billion in May.
The volume of total crude and petroleum product imports rose in May to 335.4 million barrels from 309.9 million in April. The total value rose to $5.92 billion in May from $5.49 billion.
The price of imported crude oil fell to an average $17.00 a barrel in May from $17.17 a barrel in April. The value of May crude oil imports rose to $4.60 billion from $4.29 billion.

The balance-of-payments basis for recording U.S. trade via receipts from and payments to other countries includes adjustments for military shipments, nonmonetary gold, and inland freight trade with Canada and Mexico.
Census basis data uses information collected by the U.S. Customs Service on goods shipped across U.S. borders.
